texts: My landlord, a moneylender, fasts every Monday and proudly tells the whole building, then raises our rent the next day. His shadow looks hungrier than he does. Doha?
doha on a moneylender who fasts for show while squeezing the poor, with his shadow of guilt
The moneylender starves the body for a day and feeds the greed for a year, and his shadow grows long with both.
A doha about the moneylender who keeps a strict fast each week and boasts of his hunger, while his long shadow falls across the debtors he has ruined, and no fasting touches the greed in his mind.
moneylender, shadow, fasting

People starve themselves on the appointed days and think the tongue's restraint is holiness, but the tongue that avoids grain still slanders, and the mind that has not been fasted from anger stays fat with sin.
My aunt is on a strict fast today and has snapped at everyone, and her tongue is sharp enough to cut the vegetables she is not eating. Doha for her?
The tongue fasts from food, but feasts on gossip.
fasting, tongue, cruelty
doha about fasting but letting the tongue say nasty things
thorn, penance, show
doha: lying on a bed of thorns for show, your mind still isn't clean
A doha on the penance of the man who lies on a bed of thorns for the crowd, wounding his body to impress the watchers, though the thorn of anger in his own mind remains unremoved.
He lies on thorns to show the world, yet carries a sharper thorn within that he will not pull out.
A man in the fair lay on a bed of thorns for hours, and people threw coins at him. He went home to count them. Kabir would laugh. A doha?
Write about the woman who keeps a fast for her family's welfare, rings the bell during her rituals for hours, and then scolds the servants, as though the vow and the bell could replace kindness.
doha: fasting vow plus ringing a bell all day and still being rude to everyone
The bell rings for the vow, the stomach is empty, but the heart is quite full of pride.
fast, bell, vow
My mother-in-law does her fast every week with a bell and a long vow, and then sits all evening telling us who in the family is a sinner. What a doha that would be
arrow, blind man, penance
doha: blind man shooting an arrow, penance aimed at nothing
The arrow of penance, loosed by a blind man, flies far from the mark of the mind.
My uncle took a vow of silence and fasting for forty days to impress the village, but he was as blind to his own anger as a blind man shooting an arrow in the dark. A doha?
A doha on the blind man who shoots the arrow of penance and vow into the dark, striking everything but the target, which is the cleansing of his own restless and greedy mind.
doha pls: fasting every week but still being greedy
hunger without humility
A doha about the people who deny themselves food on the holy days and think this makes them pure, though the hunger of the body is not the same as the hunger of the soul, nor does it teach humility.
He starves the belly and spoils the soul.
Everyone in my office who fasts on Tuesdays makes sure to announce it, and none of them is any kinder than on other days. Could you write a doha?
bell, rainbird, vow
The rainbird thirsts without announcing it, the bell rings out the vow of the proud.
A doha about the rainbird that fasts from all water but the one pure drop out of true longing, and the man who rings a bell to announce his fast and vows for the world to see.
A neighbour rings a bell every time she starts a new fast and tells the building, while the rainbird on our wire seems more patient in its thirst. A doha?
doha: rainbird really fasts, the man ringing a bell about his vow is just showing off
doha: fasting with a sword in hand and salt in the wound, vow to hurt others

A doha for the man who fasts and takes a solemn vow with a sword at his side, vowing revenge, while he refuses salt in his food and all the other pleasures, as if austerity and violence could live together.
sword, salt, vow
He gives up salt and keeps his sword, and calls the vow holy.
My neighbour has been fasting without salt for a month and brags about it, then threatened his brother with a sword over some land. A doha on that?
Every month my grandfather observes a strict fast in the house, and everyone has to be quiet, otherwise he curses them for disturbing his penance. A doha?
house, fasting, strict
A doha on the fasting householder who turns his house into a prison of rules and silence for the sake of his vow, making everyone around him suffer for his own supposed holiness.
The house goes hungry with him, and no one in it is any holier for his vow.
doha about fasting at home in the house and making everyone miserable
inn, bell, vow
At the inn the vow is announced with a bell; the Lord, who lives in the silence, is not impressed.
At the inn on our trip, a fellow guest kept a loud bell on his table to mark his fast, and he refused to share the table with anyone but demanded special food. A doha?
doha: vow at the inn with a bell, showing off his fast
A doha about the guest at the inn who keeps an elaborate fast with a ringing bell, demanding special meals from the host and staring down those who eat, as if his vow made him better than them.
doha: weaver's loom keeps working, fasting people just show off
The weaver in our lane works at his loom through the day without eating much, but he doesn't call it a fast or boast about it, unlike the others. A doha?
weaver's loom, honest hunger
A doha on the weaver at his loom who goes hungry without ever calling it a fast, and the man who fasts for a day and puts it in front of everyone, wondering which of them is truly spare.
The weaver at his loom has honest hunger; the proud man's hunger is a loud ornament.
My grandmother observes a fast on special days, applies sandalwood paste to the idol, and then criticises all of us for not being devout enough. Doha for her?
Sandalwood on the idol's brow and a fast on the stomach, but a mind with no coolness in it.
doha: fasting and sandalwood but still judgmental
Write a doha on the person who keeps a fast and applies sandalwood paste and sits very straight, expecting admiration, while the heat of judgement burns within and no sandalwood can cool it.
fasting, sandalwood, pride
doha: thief takes a vow to fast but doesn't stop stealing, with his sword
A local gang leader with a sword took a vow to fast every Friday and have the whole street know it, but he is still a thief. A doha?
The thief takes a vow of fasting and keeps the sword; it is the mind that starves of mercy.
thief, sword, vow
A doha on the thief who takes a solemn vow of fasting and continues to carry his sword and rob the helpless, as though a day without food could wash away a lifetime of cruelty.
Write about the priest who orders his followers to take difficult vows and fasts, while keeping himself in a comfortable cage of luxury, where the vow is for others and the feast is for himself.
Our priest told every family to do forty days of fasting and left for a hotel stay with his own family, saying the cage of his duties wore him down. A doha?
The priest shuts them in a cage of vows, and himself in a cage of comfort.
doha: priest demands fasting from others but eats royally himself, in a cage of luxury
priest, cage, vows
A doha about the person who starves his body for a vow and sees his own shadow grow thin, believing he is purifying himself, though the shadow of a proud mind does not grow thin with the body.
After two weeks of fasting my friend looked thin as a shadow, but still acted proud as ever and criticised those who ate. A doha for him?
doha: fasting makes you thin like a shadow but not a better person
The body thins like a shadow at evening, but the pride stays tall.
shadow, fasting, pride
door, fasting, pride
My neighbour sits at his door on fast days looking very pale and sighing so everyone will ask him what's wrong, so that he can tell them about his fast. A doha?
doha: sitting at the door looking weak to show off your fast
He sits at the door pale and sighing, hoping the world will ask about his hunger.
A doha on the man who waits at his door on days of fasting with a sad, pale face, hoping the neighbours will praise his austerity, as if the Lord only counted his vows when others did.
starving for show
What the belly misses, the pride devours; what the mind needs, no fast provides.
My friend took a fast for a month to prove he was devout to his in-laws, and then dined out on his last day with great relish. Doha?
write a doha about people who fast for attention
A doha on the person who takes a fast not out of love for the Lord but out of a wish to be admired by others, parading his thinness in front of the neighbours like a prize.
doha: fasting beside a stone idol hoping it will bless you
He fasts before the stone, and the stone does not feed him; the Lord is not in the stone.
My cousin fasted for a week in front of a stone image, promising to eat only when it answered his wish. Hunger was the only thing that answered. A doha?
A doha on the one who keeps a harsh fast before a stone and swears not to eat until it speaks, in the belief that his hunger will move a thing that has never moved.
fasting, stone
physician, fasting, show
The physician told my uncle his fasting was harming his health, but he said the vow mattered more than his life, and did it for the village to see. A doha?
doha: even the physician says starving yourself is not holy
The physician warns the fasting body, but the proud mind will not listen.

A doha on the physician who tells the faster that his vow is harming him, and the faster who ignores him, vowing even to die for the show of devotion, though the Lord asks for the cleansing of the mind.
The rich man in the palace on the hill fasts publicly every festival, while the tailor who sews his clothes with a needle goes without a meal every day and is never praised. A doha?
A doha on the lord of the palace who observes the great fasts with ceremony and applause while the humble tailor with his needle fasts through the year in poverty without a single word of praise.
doha: palace man fasts for show, tailor with a needle fasts for real out of poverty
palace, needle, fasting
The palace fasts with fanfare; the needle fasts in poverty, and only one is truly hungry.
thread, one-string lute, vow
Our wandering singer with a one-string lute took a vow to eat only once a day and ties a thread around his wrist to count each day. He tells everyone. A doha?
doha: one-string lute singer and a vow thread and showing off his fast
A thread round the wrist to count the vow, a one-string lute to announce it, and the mind not bound to the Name.
A doha on the singer with a one-string lute who ties a sacred thread to mark each day of his vow and sings of his own sacrifices, while his heart has not changed at all.
My friend gave up sweets for a month, announced it daily, and after the month ended she ate a whole box in one night. Did the vow cleanse her? A doha
For a month she gave up sweets and gave nothing else; on the last day she made up for it all.
doha on giving up something for a vow and going back to it
vow, then relapse
A doha on vows taken for a season and dropped at the end, as the person who gives up a pleasure for a month only to return to it more hungrily, having learned nothing about the desire itself.
date palm, yogi, penance
A doha about the yogi who stands for years beside a date palm in a vow of penance, with his arms raised till they wither, whose fruit of austerity is no sweeter than the date, which he never reaches.
The yogi raises his arm in penance beside the date palm that gives fruit to all, and his arm withers.
In our region there's a yogi who has kept one arm raised for years beside a date palm, and tourists take his photo. I don't see how it cleans his mind. A doha?
doha: yogi doing penance next to a date palm, wasting his body
Dew hangs on the grass at dawn, soon gone, like the vows of the one who stays at the inn of the body for a night.
dew, inn, vow
doha: dew vanishes by noon, like vows made at the inn
A doha on the vow taken in the early morning like dew on the grass, glistening with promise and gone by noon, as quickly as a guest leaves an inn, leaving no trace of change behind.
At the inn on our pilgrimage, a fellow guest vowed at dawn to give up anger, and by noon he was shouting at the cook. The dew had barely dried. Doha?
A doha on the blind man who vows to fast and perform hard penance every night under the stars, never seeing that the real darkness is in his mind and no vow can bring light unless he looks inward.
doha: blind man fasting under the stars hoping for light
A blind man in our village fasts in the courtyard under the stars each week, and people praise his penance, though he has never looked within. A doha?
Under the stars the blind man fasts, and calls the dark his penance.
blind man, stars, fasting
doha: why do people starve themselves for God
What god is pleased by an empty stomach, when the pure heart is hungry only for truth?
My aunt starves for a week at each festival and then falls ill, and the whole family has to care for her. She says it's devotion. What would Kabir say?
A doha on the ones who starve themselves for a god they say loves them, and who believe that suffering is the only coin the Lord accepts, though He has asked only for love.
starving for God
The heron fasts at the water's edge, the cloud fasts from rain; but the heron's patience is hunger and not holiness.

A doha about the heron that stands without food at the water's edge, looking like a saint at a fast, while really waiting for its meal, like those who fast for show and expect blessings under the cloud.
heron, cloud, fake fast
doha: heron looks like it's fasting, the cloud too, but both want something
My neighbour looked like a heron as he stood in the courtyard under the clouds, fasting in a loud display, and I knew he wanted the street's admiration. A doha?
doha: crow doesn't fast, he eats leaf scraps, honest vs a fasting hypocrite
crow, leaf, vow

A doha on the crow which eats what it finds without pretending to fast and the faster who eats a single leaf for show in public and gorges himself in private, the crow being the more honest of the two.
The crow eats what it finds; the faster eats one leaf in public and a feast in private.
A neighbour fasted in public and ate a leaf of tulsi, but I saw a crow stealing food from his kitchen, and I wonder whose fast it was. A doha?
doha: fasting without a clean heart is useless
My cousin fasts on Thursdays and gambles on Fridays. A doha for him please?
A doha for the one who fasts to please the Lord on the appointed days and spends the rest of the days in lies, gambling and anger, as if the Lord kept account of hunger and not of the heart.
Fast from anger and from greed; the belly's hunger cleans no soul.
fast, gambling, hypocrite
doha: a vow without effort to change is empty
A doha on the vow taken with great promises on a festive day and broken the next, which leaves the person exactly where he began, for the change a vow requires cannot be made by a promise alone.
A vow is a sapling that needs the soil of effort.
Each new year my brother takes a hundred vows, and each year he breaks them all before the end of January. Doha for him?
broken vows
He seeks the paras, the alchemist's touch, through fasting and penance, and washes the washerman's cloth of his own mind in hunger.
The washerman in our lane fasts to find the paras, the alchemist's touch, he says, and tells everyone, though I think the only thing he is washing is his pride. Could you write a doha?
paras, washerman, fast
doha: fasting to find the paras, the alchemist's touch, a washerman cleaning pride

A doha on the man who fasts and does penance to find the paras, the alchemist's touch, while the washerman beside him washes clothes in honest work, and finds more truth in his labour than the seeker in his fasting.
The old tree in our colony has a ribbon tied round it by women who fast for their husbands' long life, and then they quarrel loudly under it. A doha?
The women fast and tie their wishes round the tree, and the tree stands silent in its patience.
fast, tree, wish
doha: fasting under a tree for a wish, tree gives without fasting
A doha about the fast kept beneath a great tree, the vows made and wishes tied to its trunk with ribbons, while the tree, which gives shade to all without a vow, knows what it means to give.
milk, crow, fasting
On fast days my neighbour drinks only milk and sits proudly on the porch, and a crow steals the sweets from his plate, and he curses the poor crow. A doha?
doha: fasting on milk only and cursing a crow, what a joke
A cup of milk is a feast to the crow who knows true hunger, and the proud faster mocks the crow.
A doha about the faster who lives on milk alone and calls it hard austerity, while the crow who finds a hard crust to eat in the street is the one who has truly known hunger.
doha: fasting won't change you if your heart is closed
closed heart, open stomach
A doha on the faster who refuses food for the sake of holiness, yet keeps his heart closed to the poor at his gate who would be grateful for the meal he refuses and could use his kindness.
The plate is empty, but the hand is closed.
My neighbour's family fasts once a week, but when a hungry child came to their gate, they sent him away. Could you write a doha for them?
doha: chakor bird stays up all night in love, but humans fast for a day and think they're devoted
chakor bird, true fasting
A doha on the chakor bird that spends its nights gazing at the heavens in true longing, forgetting hunger and sleep, and the man who fasts for a day and thinks that is devotion enough.
The chakor bird forgets its food in love; the man remembers his vow in vanity.
My friend fasted for a day and told me the chakor bird could learn something from her devotion, though the bird forgets food from real longing. A doha for her?
A doha on the yogi who declares that he eats nothing and drinks nothing, who sits publicly for months in a vow of fasting, while a hidden disciple brings him food by night.
yogi, fasting, fraud
doha: yogi says he doesn't eat, but he does secretly
The yogi says he lives on air, and his disciple feeds the air in the dark.
A yogi in our area claimed he hadn't eaten for years, and then a villager saw a disciple secretly bringing him meals. Kabir would have loved that story. A doha?
doha: shroud like clothes and fasting, acting dead but not changed
He wraps in a shroud, he fasts as if already dead, yet the living greed still breathes.
A doha on the man who takes a vow to live as one dead, wearing a shroud and refusing food, to impress the village, though his desires are as alive as ever.
shroud, fast, show
My uncle wore a white shroud like robe for his month long fast and posed for photos with his hungry-looking face. The next week he bought a new TV. A doha?
A doha on the person who takes a vow of silence and fasting and counts the days on prayer beads, as though each bead were a coin paid into some heavenly bank, and not a day to be lived.
doha: counting prayer beads for vow days like a debt
prayer beads, vow, counting
He counts the days of the vow on his prayer beads, but the days of his anger go uncounted.
My aunt counts the days of her vow on prayer beads and gets angry if anyone disturbs her counting. Doha for her?
A doha for the priest who preaches long fasts, standing like a heron at the edge of the pond, looking very devout, though his eyes are fixed on the offerings the faithful will bring.
Our priest looks like a heron in his stillness during the fast, but his eyes follow every plate of offerings that comes in. A doha for him?
priest, heron, fasting
doha: priest fasting like a heron, waiting for offerings
The priest stands like the heron, eyes closed, fasting, and waiting for the offerings.
My brother took a vow to climb a hill barefoot to be forgiven, and complained the whole way and was rude to the porters. A doha?
A doha about the man who walks barefoot for miles on a vow, hurting his feet and boasting of it, though he is no closer to forgiving his enemies or asking forgiveness of those he has harmed.
doha: barefoot vow without a changed heart
barefoot vow
He tortured the soles of his feet, but the sole of his soul remained untouched.
He walks through the fire of penance with a proud step, yet the fire in his heart is never put out.
fire, penance, pride
doha: walking on fire as penance, still angry
A doha on the one who sits between fires in the summer heat as a penance for sins, enduring the pain to be seen by all, though the fire of anger in his heart is left to burn.
At the fair, a man walked over fire to fulfil a vow, and afterwards got into a brawl with the man selling him water. A doha for him?
The priest fasts and the thief fasts; one steals with his mouth, one with his hands.
The priest in our area fasts every second day and then charges a fee for every blessing, while the thief who robbed the corner store prayed and fasted too. A doha?
A doha on the priest and the thief who both keep a fast on a vow, the priest to look holy and the thief to be forgiven, though neither has stopped taking from the helpless.
priest, thief, fasting
doha: priest and thief both fast, no difference
A doha about the rainbird which fasts from all water but the single drop of rain, out of true longing, and the man who fasts as a rule and complains of thirst, never asking what he truly hungers for.
doha: rainbird's thirst is honest, human fasting is for show
My aunt complains the whole day when she fasts, while the rainbird outside our window waits all season for one drop without a word. A doha?
The rainbird thirsts in silence and the faster thirsts in speech.
rainbird, true thirst
touchstone, yogi, fasting
doha: touchstone test for a yogi's fasting
Rub the yogi's fast on the touchstone of conduct, and see how little worth is in it.
A famous yogi who fasts for months was tested by a skeptical journalist and his conduct fell apart like a cheap alloy on a touchstone. A doha?
A doha on the touchstone that tests the worth of a yogi's fasting and penance, and finds that true purity is not there, though the show of austerity is bright and loud.
doha: stop starving, start serving
Better a full plate shared with the hungry than an empty plate vowed to the sky.
serve, don't starve
A doha for the faster who gives up his meal and sits in hunger for the Lord, who would be better served if he gave that meal to a hungry stranger and took his vow of kindness instead.
During Ramadan style fasting season in our colony some families waste vast amounts of food at night after their day's fast, while the street kids go hungry. A doha?
My dad does a rigid fast every week, and he nags the family to do the same, but he doesn't seem happier or kinder for it. A doha?
doha: fasting makes people grumpy not holy
A doha on the man who imposes a fast on himself and his family, forcing every household member to share his rules, making everyone irritable, and calling the misery spiritual progress.
The fast makes the home sour, and he calls the sourness holiness.
grumpy faster
A doha on the vow taken at the sacred place with great drama before a crowd, then broken quietly in the privacy of one's room, where the Lord, who sees every secret, is the only witness.
doha: vow in public, break it in private
public vow, private lapse
What is sworn aloud is forgotten in whispers.
My colleague took a vow in front of the whole office to quit smoking and I saw him sneaking out for one behind the building two hours later. A doha?
The snake charmer in our town fasts on certain days to protect his snake and show his devotion, but he starves the snake the rest of the time. A doha?
He fasts for the snake's sake and starves the snake for his own.
doha: snake charmer fasts for show, snake starves
A doha on the fasting snake charmer who pretends his vow is a sacrifice for the creature, though the poor snake is half starved and the vow is only a show for the crowd that pays.
snake, fasting

For the festival the community built a bridge of flowers and the head of the committee, wearing a white shroud-like robe, did a very showy fast, while the real bridge in the village has been broken for years. A doha?
The bridge of flowers is built for the vow, and the shroud-clad leader's real bridge stays broken.

A doha on the one who wears a white shroud for his fast and builds a fancy bridge of flowers for the festival, while the real bridge that villagers need lies broken, and his vow does nothing for them.
bridge, shroud, vow
doha: shroud and bridge, fasting for show, real needs ignored
doha: fire and door, the vow to keep the door closed to the poor
door, fire, fasting
A man in our locality sits in front of his door with a burning fire on his fast days and tells everyone his vow, yet never opens the door to the hungry. A doha?
He fasts by the fire of the door and keeps it closed on those who are hungry.
A doha on the one who sits at his door beside a fire on fast days, vowing not to eat, who keeps the door shut against the hungry who come hoping for the meal he refuses.
